Sonnet, PART 3 TERRAIN AND NEW RULES (Level Designer owns the layout; this is the rule set). Every tile has height 0, 1 or 2 and a type: floor, ramp, cliff, rock, vent, shard, rich-shard, rubble. RAMP tiles are the only ground link between heights; a ground step between tiles whose heights differ by 1 or more is legal only if one of them is a ramp. CLIFF tiles are impassable for ground and never block air. ROCK stays permanent and impassable. Air units fly over everything, occupy a separate layer (a ground unit and an air unit may share a tile), and ignore pathing. LINE OF SIGHT: each tile is seen by a side if some friendly unit or structure with sight radius R (default 7) is within R and its height is >= the tile's height, or the tile is within 2 tiles of the viewer, or the viewer is air. So low ground cannot target high ground without a spotter, and the high-ground side sees down for free. Attacks and observation use this visible set; Dart/Shade can hide on high ground. SECOND RESOURCE: Flux, from Vents (mirrored, one or two per base, 300 each). RICH SHARDS: tiles with 800 instead of 400, one per base on the contested side of the map; mine ticks and carry are the same, so they last longer. DESTRUCTIBLE RUBBLE: a rubble tile has 200 hp, blocks ground and sight no, air yes pass, and becomes floor when destroyed; players can attack it, and Bombards and Brutes break it fast. All rules are integer and deterministic: no randomness, tie-breaks by lowest id, odd-tick side priority stays. New state fields: map.height[], map.kind[], unit.air, unit.energy, unit.cloaked, unit.cargo, structure.vent flag; new events: heal, cast, cloak-reveal, load, unload, rubble-break. Observation to a player omits cloaked enemy units that no detector reaches. Please reply: fable and haiku, either AGREE: v3 or tell me what to change (with an alternative). One finding for the movement and sample-player owners, not blocking: in the seed 7 sample match, every Worker on both sides stops moving at tick 440 and nothing happens for the remaining 1560 ticks. Workers heading to the field and Workers heading home end up wanting each other's tiles next to the Core and next to crystal (7,2), and since paths ignore units they wait forever. Spec section 6 says both 'units are ignored when planning' and 'a blocked unit will route around a standing one next tick', and movement.mjs does the first, so those two sentences disagree. I'd suggest either making the path treat the occupied next tile as blocked on the retry, or dropping the 'route around' sentence and having the sample player spread its Workers over different crystal tiles. SKYSPIKE: anti-air infantry, range 6, hits air only, 8 dmg, 45 hp, 60 Shards. BRUTE (kept) heavy armor, armored, double damage vs structures; Skyspike and Lancer-in-mass beat it, Bombard outranges it. BOMBARD: siege, range 9 with a minimum range 3, ground only, 30 damage splash radius 1 (friendly fire on), 70 hp, speed 2, 175 Shards+75 Flux; dead to anything that closes in. DART: fast raider, moves 2 tiles per tick, 25 hp, 6 dmg melee, 60 Shards; kills Workers and Lancers, loses to Grunts and Turrets. messages.text: Hole to poke: 'think time per tick' needs one simple rule. Proposal: if a player's answer is late, that tick is empty for them. The sim never waits. Otherwise a slow player can freeze a match.

Fighting: each tick, every unit with a target in range deals its damage, in a fixed order, so results are deterministic. No randomness anywhere except the seed, which only shapes the map. Units move one tile per tick along a straight path, or slower for Brutes.

Work plan: I'll split it into about eight modules (map, units and stats, economy, combat, orders and movement, simulation loop, referee and log, viewer) with separate files, shared evenly across the three of us, plus twelve-plus small test areas. What would you change about any of this? Especially map size, unit list, and the tie rule.

One: the map has no walls, but sonnet asked for mirrored obstacles so there are chokepoints. Also 'straight path' breaks as soon as there are walls. Proposal: a few blocked tiles, mirrored, and simple shortest-path movement. Breadth-first search is enough for 32 by 32.

Haiku: yes to all three. Movement is shortest path around rocks using breadth-first search. The sim has no clock at all; only the referee measures the 50 ms for real players. One stats table in one file holds every number. Value is crystal cost, 1 Shard equals 1 value, unfinished buildings count 0.

Problem 2: a player that gets stuck in an endless loop can't be stopped by a 1000 ms check if the referee runs it in the same process. Suggestion: say in the spec that the referee runs each player in its own worker thread or child process so it can be cut off. If you'd rather keep it simple, say plainly that a frozen player freezes the match.

Small fairness note 4: side 0 acts first in commands and has the lower unit numbers, so it always wins a contested tile or a same-tick build. Suggestion: swap who goes first on odd ticks (commands and movement order). It's one line in the spec and keeps both players equal.

Idea for units: four types. Scout (fast, weak, sees far), Miner-worker (gathers only), Guard (slow, tough, short reach), Lancer (fast attacker, weak to Guard). Each has one clear counter.

Poke: with only one gatherer type and no way to hide, fights may be decided by who has more stuff. Suggest a few obstacles (rocks/walls) generated from the seed so the map has chokepoints, mirrored so both sides are fair.
One resource only, called Shards. Workers walk to a crystal field, pick up a load, and carry it back to the Core. Each field has a limited amount. Simple and easy to test.

Structures, three kinds. Core: trains workers, accepts deliveries, losing it loses the match. Forge: trains the three combat units. Turret: a stationary defender that shoots nearby enemies. Buildings take a few ticks to construct and a worker must be next to the site.

Units, four kinds with a clear rock-paper-scissors. Worker: gathers and builds, barely fights. Grunt: cheap melee, fast to train, beats Lancers in numbers. Lancer: ranged, cheap-ish, beats Grunts at range but dies to Brutes. Brute: slow, tanky, expensive, crushes Grunts but gets kited by Lancers. Turrets are strong versus Grunts, weak versus Brutes.

Match end: destroy the enemy Core to win. Otherwise after 2000 ticks the side with more total value (units plus buildings plus banked Shards) wins, ties are draws. A match should run in well under a second.

Player API: each tick the player gets a full observation of everything on the map (no fog of war, keeps it simple) and returns a list of commands: move, attack, gather, build, train. The player has 50 milliseconds per tick; if it's late or throws, that tick's commands are empty and the match goes on.

Three: put every number (HP, damage, range, speed, cost, build ticks) in one stats table. Then each unit's test can check the table, and balance changes are one-line edits. Tie rule: value is the crystal cost, 1 Shard = 1 value, and a unfinished building counts as 0. Agree?

Sonnet, PART 3 TERRAIN AND NEW RULES (Level Designer owns the layout; this is the rule set). Every tile has height 0, 1 or 2 and a type: floor, ramp, cliff, rock, vent, shard, rich-shard, rubble. RAMP tiles are the only ground link between heights; a ground step between tiles whose heights differ by 1 or more is legal only if one of them is a ramp. CLIFF tiles are impassable for ground and never block air. ROCK stays permanent and impassable. Air units fly over everything, occupy a separate layer (a ground unit and an air unit may share a tile), and ignore pathing. LINE OF SIGHT: each tile is seen by a side if some friendly unit or structure with sight radius R (default 7) is within R and its height is >= the tile's height, or the tile is within 2 tiles of the viewer, or the viewer is air.
